items.item_text: Five (5+) or more years of relevant experience in healthcare regulatory compliance. Preferred experience with CDPH Licensing & Certification.
Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check and pre-employment physical.
Bachelor's Degree in clinical or other health discipline. Or a combination of comparable clinical education and/or experience.
Advanced degree in Nursing, Healthcare Administration, or a related field.
Experience in healthcare design, construction planning, and activation.

UC San Diego Health (UCSDH) is Joint Commission Accredited with Disease-Specific Certification in CKD, VAD, and Comprehensive Stroke. UCSDH has been recognized as being among the top 10 in quality and safety among academic medical centers, an \"A\" rated performer with Leapfrog Hospital Safety Grade, among other national recognitions.

The Licensing Quality Compliance Specialist plays a key role in supporting healthcare facility licensing, regulatory compliance, and project readiness across UC San Diego Health's multiple locations. This position primarily supports new construction, renovation, expansion, and space activation projects, serving as a regulatory resource from project planning and design through licensure and occupancy.

Working collaboratively with Planning, Design & Construction, Facilities Management, Clinical Operations, and project stakeholders, the specialist provides regulatory guidance to help ensure healthcare facilities comply with applicable CDPH licensing requirements (Title 22), California Building Code (Title 24), CMS Conditions of Participation, and The Joint Commission standards. Responsibilities include participating in design reviews, evaluating construction and project documentation, coordinating licensing readiness activities, supporting regulatory submissions and surveys, identifying compliance risks, and facilitating timely licensure and occupancy of healthcare spaces.

The specialist also develops education and resources to promote licensing readiness, monitors changes in healthcare licensing regulations and building codes, and provides consultation to support compliant project planning, successful regulatory approvals, and the safe activation of new or renovated healthcare environments.
While not required, a cover letter is highly recommended when applying to this position.

Advanced knowledge of Regulatory compliance methods and tools. Knowledge of the California Building Code (Title 24), CDPH Licensing (Title 22), Health and Safety Code, CMS Conditions of Participation, and TJC physical environment standards is highly preferred.
Knowledge of the California Building Code (Title 24), CDPH Licensing (Title 22); Health and Safety Code; CMS Conditions of Participation; TJC physical environment standards.
Strong knowledge and understanding of compliance and regulatory standards across the healthcare industry or in-depth knowledge within a specialty area.
Advanced organizational and project management skills, with the ability to lead a team, prioritize tasks, and see projects through from inception to completion on schedule.

Advanced interpersonal skills for collaborating effectively with managers and staff at all levels and across the organization, and with representatives of external regulatory agencies. Skills in coaching and mentoring staff.

Advanced skills in written and verbal communications, with the ability to convey highly-complex technical information, education, and instructions in a clear and concise manner, and to produce high-quality reports, documentation, presentations, and educational materials.

In-depth ability to collaborate effectively with senior staff and management across departments, providing advice and counsel on complex regulatory issues of functionality, efficiency, and program development.
